cards.text: This is Psalm 145, a psalm of praise from David, Israel's king. David's got the throne, the crown, the whole royal setup. And the first thing he does is talk straight to God and call Him 'my God and King.'

cards.question: King David has a King of his own. How long does David say he'll bless God's name?

answers.text: For the rest of his reign

cards.question: David plans to save his praise for the big days, like feasts and victories.

cards.text: Every day, not just the big ones. Then David turns from talking to God to talking about Him: "Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised; His greatness is unsearchable."

cards.question: David says the LORD's greatness is unsearchable. What does he mean?

answers.text: No one can ever reach the end of it
God keeps it hidden from His people
Only kings are able to understand it

cards.text: Friend, I lived in a junk drawer for YEARS and never found the bottom of that pile of old takeout menus, and that was a DRAWER. Now David starts thinking about who'll tell God's mighty acts after him.

cards.question: David looks way past his own lifetime. He pictures each ___ telling the next one about God's mighty acts.

cards.text: Then David says he'll meditate on God's wondrous works. Not skim them like a group chat with 400 unread messages. MEDITATE.

cards.question: David says others will proclaim the power of God's awesome deeds, and David himself will declare God's greatness too.

cards.text: They'll celebrate the fame of God's abundant goodness and sing joyfully of His righteousness. Everybody's talking, everybody's singing, and it's all about ONE God.
Then David stops telling you who's talking about God. He tells you what God is actually like.

cards.question: David describes the LORD as quick to anger but just as quick to calm down.

cards.text: "The LORD is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in loving devotion." That's close to how the LORD described Himself to Moses, way back in Exodus 34:6.

cards.question: David just said the LORD is gracious and compassionate. How far does he say the LORD's goodness reaches?

answers.text: Only to those who praise Him

cards.text: Generations of people praising God. That's already a BIG crowd. Now David widens the circle even more.

cards.question: David says only people will give the LORD thanks, and the rest of what He made stays quiet.

cards.text: All He made gives Him thanks, and His saints bless Him. Then those saints open their mouths and tell of the glory of His kingdom and speak of His might.

cards.question: The saints talk about God's kingdom and His might. Why do they do it?

answers.text: So people would know His mighty acts
So their enemies would be afraid
So God would reward them for it

cards.text: Now remember who's talking here. A king, with his own throne, talking about Somebody else's kingdom.

cards.question: David says God's kingdom is ___, and His dominion endures through all generations.
David says the LORD is faithful in all His words, not just some of them.
David moves from God's kingdom to what this King does for people. What does the LORD do for all who fall or are bowed down?

answers.text: He holds them up and lifts them
He waits for them to stand alone
He sends someone else to help

cards.text: Then David pictures the eyes of all looking to the LORD. Like a whole room of coworkers watching the door, waiting on the boss to walk in.

cards.question: All eyes look to the LORD. What does He give them?

cards.text: "You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing." Friend, I've got a whole mustache for hands, and I can't satisfy ONE baker who wants extra sprinkles.

cards.question: David says the LORD is righteous in His ways, but only kind to the people who earn it.

cards.text: Then David takes on a question a lot of us carry around. How close is God, really?

cards.question: Who does David say the LORD is near to?

answers.text: Those who call on Him in truth
Those who never stumble at all
Those who serve in the temple

cards.question: For those who fear the LORD, what does He do when they cry out?

answers.text: He hears them and saves them
He tests them a while longer
He tells them to wait quietly

cards.question: David draws a line between those who love the LORD and the wicked. He says the LORD preserves both groups.

cards.text: And David ends right where he started, with his own mouth declaring the praise of the LORD. 'Forever and ever' shows up again, just like in his first two lines.

cards.question: In his last line, David calls on every ___ to bless the LORD's holy name forever and ever.

findings.problem: David being Israel's king, with a throne and crown, is outside Psalm 145:1. That verse identifies the psalm as David's but does not support the added kingship details, and no reference for those details is given.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentence-length units: the statement about meditating, the group-chat comparison, and the standalone 'MEDITATE.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentence-length units: 'Generations of people praising God.', 'That's already a BIG crowd.', and the sentence about David widening the circle.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This is a who question, but the wrong answer 'Those who never stumble at all' is not a real detail from somewhere in the Bible; James 3:2 says that we all stumble in many ways. The other wrong answer, those who serve in the temple, is a real biblical detail.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.
